note: Self-contained conformance vectors. Each {receipt, options, expect} runs through any TrustLattice-conformant verifier and must yield the per-claim statuses in expect.claims. See README.md and docs/protocol/VERDICTS.md.

vectors.description: The engine golden, verified under the real sealer key with its bound six-claim envelope. Integrity is re-derived (hash + pinned signature), but the envelope is NOT covered by the receipt signature — it only names the receipt by id+hash — so every issuer attestation it marks VERIFIED is READ, not re-derived, and surfaces as NOT_CHECKED. See clean-valid-pinned-authenticated for the one case that can lift them.

does_not_attest: cumulative_total (no atomic reservation)
total_cap_scope (the total limit is per policy version, not lifetime: it is keyed to the policy hash, which includes the nonce, so it resets when a policy is superseded)
tool_class (caller-asserted; there is no tool registry in the MVP)
explicit_revocation (revocation is supersession by a higher nonce inside this ledger only)
laya (shadow mode; not consulted)
signer_trust (the signature proves which key sealed this receipt, not that the key is the engine's: a verifier checks header.signer against its own trusted list)
asset_and_chain (the owner policy does not constrain which asset or chain a spend uses)
declared_payment_fields (amount and payee are as the caller declared them; the kernel does not observe what the tool then pays)
settlement (this is an authorisation, not an observed payment)
dry_preview (this receipt is not an authorization to execute)

This is the sole path that lifts an envelope claim to VERIFIED; it still rests on trusting the channel, not on re-derivation.

vectors.description: One decision field flipped (ALLOW->DENY) without re-hashing. The recomputed hash no longer matches header.receipt_hash, so integrity FAILS AND the real envelope no longer binds (its digest is over the original bytes): it is PRESENT_UNBOUND and ignored, so nothing is "downgraded" — every read claim is fail-closed NOT_CHECKED. Contrast untrusted-signer, where the bytes are intact so the envelope stays BOUND.

Freshness overrides the read, so authorization is FAILED, not NOT_CHECKED.

vectors.description: A pin that is not 0x+64 hex. The whole pin set is rejected before any signature check (fail-safe: a garbage pin trusts nothing — it does not throw, and never falls back to the header key). The caller ASKED for a signature check that could not run, so integrity is lowered from VERIFIED to NOT_CHECKED (a typo'd pin must never read as a pass). With integrity not established, the bytes are untrusted, so every other claim is fail-closed NOT_CHECKED.
